Q: How can I bind the ng-select items to data injected into a MAT_DIALOG_DATA in Angular 21? A:

Seems issue is not with MAT_DIALOG_DATA or binding issue. The is being passed correctly.

The problem is overlay stacking with Angular 21 + CDK changes, ng-select especially with appendTo="body" renders its dropdown behind the MatDialog.

Avoid chasing change detection fixes, either remove appendTo="body" or adjust the CDK overlay config like OVERLAY_DEFAULT_CONFIG.

Q: Error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'path') when uploading files with Multer and Cloudinary A:

Diagnosis — likely causes

  • Multer didn't receive a multipart/form-data upload (so req.file is undefined). In API clients like Thunder Client you must send the request as multipart/form-data (use the "form-data" body type and a file field), not JSON or raw.

  • Field name mismatch between the name you used in the client and the name passed to upload.single(...). upload.single('image') expects the file field to be named image.

  • The route must include the multer middleware (i.e. upload.single('image')) on the POST that handles the upload.

".single(fieldname)

Accept a single file with the name fieldname. The single file will be stored in req.file."


<input id='profilePic' name='myImage' type='file'  />

var upload = multer({ storage: storage }).single('myImage');

This is not well documented but fieldname refers to input name attribute

This shows that the string passed to upload.single(...) must exactly match the file field's name attribute (or the key used in your API client).

"If you are using upload.single() (which your code shows), then the result will be in req.file, not in req.files... Also, if it's this route that you're expecting to use: router.post('/images', image.create); then, you don't have the upload() middleware installed for that route."

// you must attach multer middleware to the route
router.post('/images', upload.single('file'), image.create);

This confirms the middleware must be applied to the route that handles the upload, and that req.file (not req.files) is where a single-file upload will appear.

Quick checklist to fix your code (apply in order)

  1. Ensure the route includes multer middleware:

    • Your route already has adminRouter.post('/add-doctor', upload.single('image'), addDoctor); — good. If you changed that code elsewhere, make sure it’s present on the actual route being called.

  2. Match the field name used by the client:

    • In Thunder Client the file key must be image (because you call upload.single('image')).

    • Example: set the request body type to form-data, add a key image of type File, and choose the file to upload.

  3. Make the request as multipart/form-data (Thunder Client):

    • In Thunder Client choose Body → Form → form-data (not JSON/raw).

    • Add other form fields as key/value pairs (strings). If you send address as JSON string, you can keep it but your server expects address to be JSON-parsable.

  4. Check that req.file is used (not req.files):

    • Your controller already reads const imageFile = req.file; — correct for .single().

  5. Add defensive checks before using imageFile.path:

    • Return a helpful error if the file is missing to avoid the exception:

      if (!imageFile) {
  return res.status(400).json({ success: false, message: 'No image uploaded' });
}

  6. If using body-parsers, order doesn't usually matter with multer, but ensure you are not converting the request body before multer in a way that strips multipart boundaries. Typical Express setup:

app.use(express.json());
app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true }));
// routes that use multer will still work when upload middleware is on the route

Tips & Alternatives

If you prefer not to store files on disk, use Multer's memory storage and upload the buffer to Cloudinary:


import multer from 'multer';
const storage = multer.memoryStorage();
const upload = multer({ storage });

Then in controller:


const buffer = req.file.buffer;
// use cloudinary.uploader.upload_stream(...) to upload buffer
  • In Thunder Client / Postman you can verify the request actually contains multipart data by checking the raw request preview (or the Content-Type header includes a multipart boundary).

Next steps you can try right now

  1. In Thunder Client:

    • Body → form-data.

    • Key: image → type File → choose a file.

    • Add the other required fields as text keys.

    • Send POST to /add-doctor.

  2. Add the defensive check in your controller (see code above) so you get a clear 400 response if upload is missing.

  3. If it still fails, log req.headers['content-type'] and console.log(req.file, req.body) at the top of your controller and share the logs.

Q: How do I set redirected pipes to be non-buffered so I can use system() multiple times? A:

How do I set redirected pipes to be non-buffered so I can use system() multiple times?

Pipes are not buffered in userspace. In that sense, there is no buffering to disable. On the kernel side, pipes are pretty much nothing but buffer, and there's nothing you can (or should want to) do about it. This is in any case not directly related to calls to system().

The goal is that we must be able to initialize the subprocesses once, and simply send what commands they should execute over time without closing. At the end we print cpu-usage for each subprocess etc.

Ok, and you seem to have implemented a version of that.

I attached gdb and found that system() is stalling for child2 and chil3. My understanding from skimming the manpages is that the siblings' output pipes must be closed so they can send EOF.

Unsurprising for the particular test commands you are running there. cat with no arguments reads its standard input to the end. With that connected to the read end of a pipe, it will not see EOF, and therefore will not terminate, until the write end is closed. Note well that reading its standard input to the end is a property of cat, not of system(). There are other commands you could run that would not try to read the standard input to its end.

The assignment footnote explains this too and says we should use setvbuf (stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0); as a workaround, this is simply not working for me.

If your code is representative of what is expected for this assignment then that footnote is at best a red herring. You cannot externally set the buffering for the commands you run via system(). And your own program is not using stdout to send data through the pipes anyway, so its buffering doesn't affect that data flow even for your own program's I/O. What's more, disabling buffering has nothing to do with when or whether EOF is observed on a stream.

Online resources and manpages mainly explain how I could do it if the pipes were not required to be persistent.

That's the only way it is explained because that's the only way there is. A process reading from a pipe will not observe EOF while the write end remains open in any process.

So what to do? Maybe nothing. You should consider that what you are observing might be an expected characteristic of the program you are tasked with building, such that your example inputs are not expected to work as you thought they should. Otherwise, either the assignment is deeply flawed or you have a significant misunderstanding of the requirements.

Side note: you are making trouble for yourself by connecting the standard output of the third child to a pipe. That leaves the parent with responsibility of reading that pipe and forwarding the data to its own standard output. That is more complicated than it needs to be, and it presents practical difficulties to boot. It would be better to just avoid redirecting the third child's output in the first place, so that it writes directly to where the final output should go without the parent's mediation.

Q: get list of addresses (ansible_host) from a group of servers A:

It's not substantially different than what you already have, but I believe ansible has a built-in groups variable that you can use:

{{ ((hostvars[x].ansible_host|default(x)) for x in groups['servers']) | join(',') }}

According to the docs for groups:

A dictionary/map with all the groups in inventory and each group has the list of hosts that belong to it
